label: ex:ugb-polynomial-quotient
title: Polynomial quotient
html:
Example. Polynomial quotient

Let A be the polynomial algebra k[x_1, \ldots, x_n] and consider the ideal \mathfrak{m} = (x_1, \ldots, x_n). Taking a graded lexicographic ordering on A with x_i < x_j if i < j, the ideal \mathfrak{m}^2 has a Gröbner--Shirshov basis given by \{x_i x_j\}. Thus the quotient A/\mathfrak{m}^2 is an (n+1)-dimensional k-vector space with a basis:

A/\mathfrak{m}^2 = k\{1, x_1, \ldots, x_n\}

The fact that k was a field is not important — one would have a similar statement with the integers \mathbb{Z}, though not through classical Gröbner--Shirshov basis techniques.
